transcript: Strategic Love Play starring Heléne Yorke and Michael Zegen is a one-act comedy of a first date that seems doomed from the start. They get off on the wrong foot and almost throw in the towel immediately, but they let the next hour play out and see where it takes them. I thought the performances and the chemistry between the actors were decent, but I thought the writing was not. It kind of felt like I was watching a scene written in a college elective playwriting class. The characters are both pretty out there, which provides some cheap laughs and opportunities to unabashedly discuss the trials and tribulations of dating, but this is all at the expense of a realistic conversation which I thought would have made more sense for a small, intimate play. While some of the ideas here will surely resonate with anyone who has dealt with the modern dating scene, I have to swipe left on this one. With that, another program for my collection.
reasoning: Creator praises the performances and chemistry but criticizes the writing as amateurish and ultimately says he'd 'swipe left' on it, a clear non-recommendation.
